title: Shearwave queue resilience: adaptive windowing and tenant priority to reduce long-sequence tail latency
creator: Aisha Kaur
description: Customer escalation from two enterprise tenants (Acme Health and VelaPayments) reporting repeated SLA misses during mixed workloads. Short, latency-sensitive requests were delayed or dropped when the cluster received sporadic surges of very long-sequence generation ( >32k tokens ), leading to elevated p95/p99 tail latency. Root cause appears to be an emergent 'queue shear' phenomenon where long-sequence admissions monopolize batch windows and cause starvation of short flows across hosted, dedicated, and private topologies.
reproduction_steps: 1) Deploy a canary cluster with runtime-1.21 serving both short-chat (avg 40 tokens) and long-batch generation (adversarial 16k-48k sequences).
2) Ramp long-sequence traffic to 20% of total QPS in bursts (3-5 minute waves), keep short-chat steady at normal QPS.

3) Observe scheduler admission, batching window occupancy, and per-tenant dequeue metrics. Note progressive increase in short-request queue wait times and rare request drops when batch window locks for long inflight sequences.
4) Collect traces showing long-sequence requests holding GPU execution slots and KV cache resources for extended durations leading to starvation of small requests.
5) Reproduce on Dedicated pool and private VPC to confirm topology-agnostic behavior.
investigation_findings: - Continuous batcher admits based on a global windowing heuristic that does not adapt to skewed length distributions within the window: long sequences inflate window occupancy and effective batch capacity.

- Scheduler current fairness policy only accounts for request age and total bytes, but misses per-tenant urgency and recent short-request velocity, causing 'shear' where small flows wait behind one or two long inflight requests.
- KV cache retention and per-request execution pinning amplify the effect: long requests pin KV segments and GPU contexts leading to head-of-line dominance.
- Existing mitigation (static max_sequence cap and eviction hysteresis) reduces severity but fails under bursty long-tail waves and hurts model fidelity for customers needing long contexts.
proposed_solution: 1) Adaptive windowing: compute a dynamic admission window per-host that caps effective occupancy contributed by sequences above a configurable length threshold. The cap slides with a moving average of recent sequence length distribution.
2) Tenant-priority quotas: introduce a soft-priority budget for latency-sensitive tenants (configurable flag) that guarantees a minimum slot allocation in each admission epoch.

3) Preemptive fair-dequeue: allow preemptive eviction of the trailing portion of long inflight batches (graceful truncation) when short-request backlog crosses a high-water mark, with configurable truncation policies per model family.
4) KV-slice pinning reduction: implement per-request KV slice soft-dropping for long sequences after an N-token inactivity window to reduce resource pin-length.
5) Telemetry and automatic knob tuning: expose metrics and an automated controller to tune the adaptive window and priority budgets during rollout.
implementation_todo: - Design: finalize admission algorithm signature and config surface (Diego + Aisha).
- Scheduler: add per-epoch adaptive occupancy accounting and priority budget checks (Eng: scheduler team).
- Batcher: implement graceful truncation hooks and KV-slice soft-drop logic (Eng: runtime team).
- Config: API/console flags for tenant priority enrollment and thresholds; CLI for private deployments (Product & Console).
- E2E tests: deterministic replay scenarios for mixed-length waves and unit tests for preemptive dequeue correctness.
- Canary rollout plan and canary guardrails (observability dashboards + automatic rollback on regressions).
testing_plan: - Add synthetic workload generator producing configurable mix of short and adversarial long sequences.
- Regression tests: ensure p50/p95 for short flows do not regress beyond 5% in baseline workloads.
- Stress tests: validate under 50% long-sequence bursts that tail p99 stays within SLA targets for priority tenants.
- Chaos tests: simulate node preemption and KV-slice drops to validate graceful recovery.
- Integration: test on Hosted, Dedicated, and Private clusters (infrastructure lab).
rollback_strategy: Feature-gate all changes behind a runtime feature flag. If regressions observed during canary (tail latency increase > 15% or request error rate spike), flip feature flag off to return to existing admission behavior and roll back batcher changes progressively.
rollout_plan: 1) Merge behind feature flag and run unit/e2e tests in CI.
2) Deploy to an internal dogfood cluster (runtime-1.22) with telemetry enabled for 48 hours.
3) Canary: enable for 10% of Hosted traffic and one Dedicated customer pool for 24-72 hours with close monitoring.
4) Gradual ramp to 50% then 100% across regions if metrics remain stable.
5) For Private customers, ship as opt-in upgrade with clear release notes and recommended knobs.
monitoring_and_metrics: - Per-tenant p50/p95/p99 latency for short and long request cohorts.
- Admission window occupancy heatmap (per-epoch): fraction contributed by >threshold-length requests.
- Preemptive-truncation count and average truncated tokens per event.
- KV-slice drop frequency and recovery time.
- Error rates and model-quality deltas for truncated long requests (sampled golden-checks).
